titulo: Weekly export that separates the brand from anonymized queries
lead: The baseline is a photo. To see the movie, you need the same photo every week, in the same format. The gsc_semanal.py script does that: it separates branded, non-branded, and anonymized, and writes one row per week. Without Google credentials, the same spreadsheet by hand works.
objetivo: build the weekly export that writes total, branded, non-branded, and anonymized in one row per week.

aprende.t: INEMA's real arc: impressions go up, non-branded clicks don't
Doing the same by hand when there are no credentials

hero_alt: A shelf with binders organized by color and an open notebook showing a spreadsheet.

secoes.titulo: From the week on the dashboard to the row in the file

nos.detalhe: The dashboard lags by about 2 days. The script takes the 7 days ending the day before yesterday, so the week always closes on the same day of the week.
The same regex from lesson 1. Each query is tested against it: if it matches, it's branded; if not, it's non-branded.
Branded and non-branded come from the per-query table. Anonymized is what's left over: total minus the other two. The script also counts how many different non-branded queries showed up.
The summary grows by one row per week and per site. The non-branded file keeps each query with its page, clicks, impressions, CTR, and position: it's the raw material for lessons 4 and 5.

secoes.volta: Every week, on the same day: one more row
secoes.legenda: One row per week is little work and becomes the history the dashboard doesn't keep.

texto: The script uses your gcloud login with the Search Console read-only scope and a Google Cloud project for the quota.
If you don't have this, skip to step 4: the spreadsheet by hand gives the same result, just slower.
GSC_SITES holds the properties (e.g., sc-domain:yoursite.com). GSC_MARCA holds the regex. GSC_QUOTA_PROJ holds the quota project.
No key lives in the code.
Run it on the same day of the week. Running on consecutive days creates weeks that share days; don't add those two together.
The resumo.csv file only gains rows; nothing is deleted.

exemplo.texto: The weeks 09/27–10/03 and 09/28–10/04 share six days. Both are in the file, but the comparison uses weeks that don't overlap.

texto: In the dashboard, set a 7-day window, then use the regex filter "matches" and "doesn't match". Copy the numbers into the lesson 1 spreadsheet.

secoes.titulo: The command and the file it writes
secoes.sub: Command from the open script gsc_semanal.py. Replace what is between < > with your own. It needs a Google credential; without it, use the spreadsheet.

blocos.conteudo:
export GSC_SITES="sc-domain:<seusite.com>"
export GSC_MARCA="<seusite>|<seu nome>|<erro comum>"
export GSC_QUOTA_PROJ="<projeto-da-cota>"
python3 tools/gsc_semanal.py --dias 7 --saida dados/gsc

abas.html:
• inema.club: non-branded impressions went from 8 to 157, and non-branded queries from 3 to 51 in four weeks.
  • But the club's non-branded clicks are still at 0. New people are seeing the site; they aren't clicking yet.
  • inema.pro: the first 2 non-branded clicks, in the week of 10/05 to 10/11, from searches like "curso jev".

secoes.sub: E2 needs a week of waiting.

exercicios.texto: Fine-tune the regex from lesson 1 with at least 3 variations of your brand and the typos that show up in your queries. Log the first week, with the script or by hand.
exercicios.pronto: the summary (CSV or spreadsheet) has the first row with the three buckets, and no query with your name ended up in the non-branded bucket.

exercicios.texto: One week later, on the same day, log the second row and write one sentence comparing the non-branded numbers of the two weeks.
exercicios.pronto: there are two rows with no days in common and a sentence like "non-branded impressions went from X to Y; clicks from A to B".

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The non-branded impressions for inema.club went from 8 to 157 in four weeks, and the non-branded clicks stayed at 0. What does that tell you?
opcoes: That new people started seeing the site in search, but aren't clicking yet: the next step is to check position and title.
That it's time to buy ads.
perguntas.explica: A non-branded impression is the first signal. A click depends on position and title; that's what lessons 4 and 8 tackle.

perguntas.p: Why run the export on the same day of the week every time?
opcoes: So the weeks don't share days and the comparison is fair.
Because Google only releases data on Tuesdays.
perguntas.explica: Overlapping weeks count the same days twice. At INEMA, 09/27–10/03 and 09/28–10/04 share six days.

perguntas.p: You don't have a Google Cloud credential. Now what?
opcoes: Build the same row by hand in the dashboard, with the regex filter, 10 minutes a week.
perguntas.explica: The script only automates what the dashboard shows. The hand-made spreadsheet has the same three buckets.

opcoes: Each non-branded query with its page, clicks, impressions, CTR, and position.
perguntas.explica: It's the raw material for the next lessons: a page with impressions and no clicks (lesson 4) and a query with no owner page (lesson 5).

itens.texto: Same day, same buckets, a file that only grows.
Non-branded starts with impressions. At INEMA, 8 → 157 in four weeks, with 0 clicks on the club.
gsc_semanal.py automates it; without a credential, the dashboard gives the same number.
